candidate.answerReason: The two diagonal folds successively halve the covered area. The original square therefore has area 36 square inches, side length 6 inches, and perimeter 24 inches.

methods.label: Recover the original area
methods.explanation:
The useful observation is that each of these particular folds places two matching triangles exactly on top of one another, halving the area covered by the folded paper.

Folding \(P\) onto \(R\) makes the crease along diagonal \(QS\). The two halves of the square coincide, leaving triangle \(QRS\). To fold \(Q\) onto \(S\), the next crease runs from \(R\) to the midpoint of \(QS\), along the other diagonal of the square. By the square's symmetry, this crease divides triangle \(QRS\) into two matching triangles. The resulting figure therefore covers one quarter of the original square's area.

Unfolding doubles the area twice, so the original area is
\[
9\times2\times2=36\text{ square inches}.
\]
A square with area \(36\) has positive side length \(6\) inches, since \(6\times6=36\). Its perimeter is
\[
4\times6=\boxed{24\text{ inches}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
